Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme contained in <MATH_0002>.
Let <MATH_0003> be an algebraic stack over <MATH_0004>.
We say <MATH_0005> is a <TEXTITOPEN_0001>Deligne-Mumford stack<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if there exists
a scheme <MATH_0006> and a surjective <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism
<MATH_0007>.

<STRUCT_0001>
We will compare our notion of a Deligne-Mumford stack with
the notion as defined in the paper by Deligne and Mumford later
(see insert future reference here).

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
The category of algebraic stacks over <MATH_0001> forms a <MATH_0002>-category.
Here is the precise definition.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme contained in <MATH_0002>.
The <TEXTITOPEN_0001><MATH_0003>-category of algebraic stacks over <MATH_0004><TEXTITCLOSE_0001> is the
sub <MATH_0005>-category of the <MATH_0006>-category of categories fibred in
groupoids over <MATH_0007> (see
Categories,
Definition <REF_0001>)
defined as follows:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Its objects are those categories fibred in groupoids
over <MATH_0008> which are algebraic stacks over <MATH_0009>.
<STRUCT_0003> Its <MATH_0010>-morphisms <MATH_0011> are
any functors of categories over <MATH_0012>, as in
Categories, Definition <REF_0002>.
<STRUCT_0004> Its <MATH_0013>-morphisms are transformations between functors
over <MATH_0014>, as in
Categories, Definition <REF_0003>.
<STRUCT_0005>

<STRUCT_0001>
In other words this <MATH_0001>-category is the full sub <MATH_0002>-category of
<MATH_0003> whose objects are algebraic stacks.
Note that every <MATH_0004>-morphism is automatically an isomorphism.
Hence this is actually a <MATH_0005>-category and not just a <MATH_0006>-category.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
We will see later (insert future reference here) that this <MATH_0007>-category
has <MATH_0008>-fibre products.

<STRUCT_0004><STRUCT_0005>
Similar to the remark above the <MATH_0009>-category of algebraic stacks over <MATH_0010> is a
full sub <MATH_0011>-category of the <MATH_0012>-category of categories fibred in groupoids
over <MATH_0013>. It turns out that it is closed under
equivalences. Here is the precise statement.
